newsitem.title: POLAND: Elektrim mulls Rafako takeover. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Elektrim mulls Rafako takeover. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]

text.p: Polish industrial and trading conglamorate Elektrim SA is interested taking a majority stake in Rafako SA by purchasing shares from the boiler-maker's new share issue, Elektrim's spokesman said on Thursday.

"We are considering the purchase of a majority stake in Rafako...(and) talks are under way," Krzysztof Szczesniak told Reuters, adding that Elektrim was one of five investors eyeing Rafako's new share issue.

Rafako's financial director said the boiler-maker intended to increase its share capital by 3.2 to 8.1 million shares, which would account for 25 to 46 percent of Rafako's enlarged equity after the issue.
(Corrects to clarify that after the issue, Rafako's capital will be 25 to 46 pct larger, not that the issue accounts for 25 to 46 pct of Rafako's present shares.)

"We are likely to decide to increase share capital...during the forthcoming general shareholders' meeting on June 30," Maciej Kaczorowski told Reuters. "This is a private issue, aimed at one or two investors", he added.
Currently, the Rafako has 9,330,000 shares outstanding.
Rafako's net profit reached 665,100 zlotys in 1996 and revenues from sales constituted 366.2 million zlotys.
In 1995, Rafako plant recorded losses of 56.5 million zlotys with revenues amounting to 359.2 million zlotys.
